subject: Re: Packaging reconciliation — feature pooling & stepwise tiering
messages:
From: Sara Lee <sara.lee@mediwave.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jared Moore <jared.moore@mediwave.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Packaging question: feature pooling & stepwise tiering

Hi Ben —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the team retrospective and have two quick but important asks as we evaluate Redwood for our pilot:

1) Feature pooling: our clinical search and intake pipelines share bursty token usage. We want to understand whether we can pool certain features (embeddings + small generation hooks) across tiers so we don't pay duplicate base seat costs during pilot.

2) Stepwise tiering for pilot -> production: what does a smooth upgrade and downgrade look like? Specifically: trial anchor pricing for the first 90 days, stepwise uplift for expected Q4 production volume, and a rollback path if usage falls below the anchor.

Can you send a short mapping of options or a simple matrix we can show the finance & procurement folks? Jared will join procurement calls.

Appreciate it —
Sara Lee
VP Product Operations, MediWave Health
Sara.Lee@mediwave.com

On procurement side, they asked for SLA and simple amendment language examples — happy to loop them in for a short workshop.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lee <sara.lee@mediwave.com>
Cc: Jared Moore <jared.moore@mediwave.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question: feature pooling & stepwise tiering

Sara — thanks for laying this out. Short answer: yes, we can support both feature pooling and a structured stepwise tier path; here's a concise mapping to take to finance/procurement.

Key options (high-level):
- Shared feature pool (recommended for pilot): create a single "feature pool" seat bundle where embeddings + small-gen tokens are metered against a pooled quota rather than per-seat allocation. This reduces duplicated base seat charges during low concurrency.
- Trial anchor (90 days): a discounted committed throughput band for the pilot (e.g., 30% off list) that automatically re-evaluates at day 90 with a conversion window. We can cap the conversion uplift to a fixed percentage to avoid sticker shock.
- Stepwise upgrade: staged thresholds (e.g., 0-100k tokens/day -> Tier A; 100k-500k -> Tier B) with committed savings at each step and a 14-day notice to move. Downgrade path: monthly true-up with a 30-day grace window to avoid immediate penalty.

What I can do next:
1) Kimberly will prepare a one-page matrix showing pooled vs per-seat cost curves and an example 90-day trial-anchor amendment.
2) Propose a 45-min workshop with procurement + legal to go over the amendment language and SLA trims.

Can you share a 2‑week usage sample (tokens/day for embeddings + gen) we can model into the matrix? If you prefer, Kimberly can start from typical medtech pilot numbers and we revise after you share actuals.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0139

P.S. attaching a short checklist we use for pilot->production packaging (see attachment stub: tier-matrix-draft.xlsx).

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question: feature pooling & stepwise tiering

Sara / Ben —

I've attached an initial tier matrix (tier-matrix-draft.xlsx) and a short "trial anchor" proposal (trial-anchor-proposal.pdf). Notes below that we should call out in the matrix:

- Feature pooling definition: a named resource pool for embeddings + small-generation paths. Pooling is billed as a pooled throughput commitment with a soft cap; individual seats consume from the pool. Pool size can be reallocated monthly.
- Economies: pooling shows a 20–40% unit-cost reduction vs strict per-seat allocation at pilot volumes (example numbers in the sheet).
- Upgrade cadence: we recommend 2-step elevation for pilots moving to production (Pilot -> Ramp -> Production). Each step has an associated conversion discount and a capped uplift for the first renewal to protect budget planning.
- Downgrade safety: 30-day grace, 1x make-good in credits for sudden drops >50% in committed throughput during the first 6 months.

Action items for the workshop if procurement/legal joins:
- Agree minimal amendment language for the 90-day anchor (I drafted a short clause in the PDF).
- Confirm if MediWave needs a separate SLT for embeddings (some customers do; I put the typical language in the doc).
- Decide whether pooling is billed as throughput credits or a separate SKU.

Proposed workshop times (Pacific): Tue 2026-08-18 10:00am or Tue 2026-08-18 2:00pm. Which works for you?

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Pricing & Packaging — Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai
